entities.summary: Günther Edmund Maul was a German ichthyologist and taxidermist in Portugal. Maul came to Madeira in December 1930 to work as taxidermist at Museu Municipal do Funchal, which opened to the public in 1933. He was appointed director for the museum in 1940, a post that he held to his retirement in 1979. He, however, continued his research until shortly before his death. He started two journals and opened the museum's aquarium to the public in 1959. He also participated in several expeditions including with the French bathyscaphe Archimède in 1966 and organised the first multidisciplinary expedition to the Salvage Islands in 1963.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Günther Maul's research and expeditions significantly contributed to the understanding of marine life in the Atlantic Ocean, with his work on the Salvage Islands expedition leading to new discoveries about the region's unique biodiversity. His appointment as director of the Museu Municipal do Funchal also helped establish Madeira as a hub for scientific inquiry.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Günther Maul's research and expeditions significantly contributed to the understanding of Madeira's marine life, leading to the establishment of the museum's aquarium. His work also had a lasting impact on the island's conservation efforts.
